1. SPARKLINGSPRINGWATERHOLDINGSLTD_07_03_2002-EX-10.13-SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT — expected maintenance vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT’. The core operative clause (Section 2) grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use software and documentation. While it includes maintenance services (Section 10), the primary legal relationship is the licensing of intellectual property rights. This fits the ‘license’ subgroup perfectly.

2. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Section 1) establish confidentiality obligations, and Section 2 establishes covenants not to compete, non-solicitation of customers, and non-inducement of employees. While it references a Franchise Agreement, this specific document is the restrictive covenant agreement between the franchisee and its personnel, fitting the ‘non_compete_no_solicit’ subtype perfectly.

3. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses define a joint venture relationship. Section 4.1 states: ‘The parties will be joint venturers only as to those activities that they jointly undertake for the AMR market…’. The agreement details joint development of products (Section 3.1), joint ownership of IP developed during the project, coordinated marketing and sales rights, and profit-sharing mechanisms based on net/gross proceeds. While it contains elements of development and license, the core legal structure described is a collaboration/joint venture for specific market activities, distinct from a simple affiliate referral program or pure development contract. Confidence is capped at 0.85 due to the title mismatch (‘Affiliate’) creating ambiguity between an affiliate agreement and a joint venture/collaboration agreement.

4. CardlyticsInc_20180112_S-1_EX-10.16_11002987_EX-10.16_Maintenance Agreement1 — expected maintenance vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Software License, Customization and Maintenance Agreement’ and functions as a formal contract between Cardlytics, Inc. and Bank of America. The operative clauses primarily establish the grant of a nonexclusive, worldwide license to use software (Section 2.0), define intellectual property ownership, and set forth terms for maintenance and support. While it includes provisions for customization (development) and maintenance (service), the core legal relationship is the licensing of existing IP/software, fitting the ‘license’ subtype best among the available options.

5. LOYALTYPOINTINC_11_16_2004-EX-10.2-RESELLER AGREEMENT — expected reseller vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘RESELLER AGREEMENT’ and defined as a ‘Distribution Agreement’. The operative clauses (Section 1) grant Schoolpop the right to resell AEIS’s stored value cards (‘Cards’) to clients. Section 2 grants exclusivity for resale in a specific marketplace. The agreement details inventory management, ordering processes, payment terms for purchasing inventory, and marketing rights fees associated with the distribution/resale relationship. This fits the definition of a Distributor Agreement perfectly.

6. LegacyEducationAllianceInc_20200330_10-K_EX-10.18_12090678_EX-10.18_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled a ‘Development Agreement’ but the operative clauses (Section 2) grant an exclusive license to use Intellectual Property (‘Licensed IP’) and Marks. The core obligation of LEA is to operate a business using this licensed IP, paying royalties based on sales. While there are development components (creating educational materials), the primary legal mechanism is the licensing of T&B’s IP (name, likeness, trademarks, copyrights) to LEA for commercial exploitation. This fits the definition of a License Agreement. It is not a pure development agreement because the focus is on exploiting existing IP rather than creating new IP from scratch under a development plan, nor is it a distributor agreement as LEA is operating a branded business rather than just reselling goods.

7. QBIOMEDINC_04_08_2020-EX-99.1-JOINT FILING AGREEMENT — expected joint_venture vs predicted other (compliance_filing, conf 0.95) — mode: function_over_form

The document is explicitly labeled ‘EXHIBIT 99.1’ and titled ‘JOINT FILING AGREEMENT’. Its sole purpose is to facilitate the joint filing of Schedule 13G with the SEC pursuant to Rule 13d-1(k) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. While it contains agreement language (‘The undersigned hereby agree’), its substantive function is strictly tied to regulatory compliance and securities law filings, making it a compliance filing rather than a standalone commercial contract.

8. SPRINGBANKPHARMACEUTICALS,INC_04_08_2020-EX-99.A-JOINT FILING AGREEMENT — expected joint_venture vs predicted other (compliance_filing, conf 0.95) — mode: function_over_form

The document is explicitly titled ‘EXHIBIT A JOINT FILING AGREEMENT’ and states it is filed ‘In accordance with Rule 13d-1(k) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934’. Its primary function is to facilitate the joint filing of a Schedule 13G (a regulatory compliance document) with the SEC. While it contains agreement language between parties, its substantive form and purpose are strictly tied to regulatory compliance filings rather than a standalone commercial contract.

**1. LejuHoldingsLtd_20140121_DRS (on F-1)_EX-10.26_8473102_EX-10.26_Content License Agreement2** — expected license vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: other_fallback

The document is explicitly titled ‘MUTUAL TERMINATION AGREEMENT’ and contains standard contractual recitals, consideration language, and operative clauses to terminate a prior Domain Name License Agreement. Its substantive form is a termination instrument rather than a specific commercial family (e.g., license, distribution, or service), making ‘other’ the correct subtype. The format, governing law, counterparts, and signature blocks clearly identify it as a formal contract.

2. ElPolloLocoHoldingsInc_20200306_10-K_EX-10.16_12041700_EX-10.16_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted franchise (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘FRANCHISE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ and contains standard franchise machinery, including references to the Franchisor/Franchisee relationship, Franchise Disclosure Document, individual Franchise Agreements for each developed unit, trademark/system usage rights, and territorial development schedules. These operative clauses firmly place it within the franchise family.

3. EmeraldHealthBioceuticalsInc_20200218_1-A_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_11987205_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted consulting (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Consulting and Product Development Agreement’ establishing an ongoing advisory relationship between a biotech company and a scientist. Operative clauses (Article 2) detail Dr. Murray’s responsibilities to provide guidance, scientific validation, and product development services in exchange for monthly fees, equity, and royalties. While it includes development and IP components, the substantive core is the provision of professional consulting and advisory services, aligning best with the consulting family. The hybrid title and mixed obligations warrant a moderate-high confidence score.

4. EtonPharmaceuticalsInc_20191114_10-Q_EX-10.1_11893941_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Exclusive License and Product Development Agreement’ between two pharmaceutical companies. It contains a clear grant of exclusive license rights (Section 2), extensive royalty and licensing fee structures tied to net sales (Section 6), patent prosecution and litigation responsibilities (Section 7), and standard contractual boilerplate. While it includes product development and regulatory registration obligations (Section 3), the core economic mechanism and primary subject matter revolve around licensing fees, commercial milestones, and royalties, making it substantively a license agreement. The hybrid nature of the title and clauses warrants a proportionally lower confidence score.

**5. ImperialGardenResortInc_20161028_DRS (on F-1)_EX-10.13_9963189_EX-10.13_Outsourcing Agreement** — expected outsourcing vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement between a resort developer and an architectural firm detailing planning, design, environmental assessment, and construction monitoring obligations. It contains standard contractual elements (scope of work, fee structure, payment milestones, duties, term, and dispute resolution). Although titled ‘Outsourcing Contract,’ the substantive obligations constitute professional architectural and engineering services, aligning best with the ‘service’ subtype rather than business-process outsourcing or pure product development.

6. Zounds Hearing, Inc. - MANUFACTURING DESIGN MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted manufacturing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Manufacturing, Design and Marketing Agreement.’ Its operative clauses overwhelmingly govern the manufacturing of hearing aids, detailing purchase orders, product costing, per-unit royalties, delivery and shipping terms, tooling/NRE charges, inventory management, and FDA regulatory compliance. References to design and joint marketing are either ancillary or explicitly defer specific terms to separate agreements. Thus, the substantive core and operative machinery align definitively with the manufacturing family.

7. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement.’ The operative provisions establish an exclusive distribution framework, appointing one party as the exclusive distributor, granting ‘Distribution Rights,’ detailing sub-distributor appointments, purchase obligations, net sales definitions, and royalty/milestone structures. Although the title references licensing and marketing, and the agreement contains related covenants, the substantive commercial machinery centers on the distribution and resale of products within a defined territory, aligning best with the distributor family. Confidence is moderated to 0.85 due to the explicit three-family hybrid title.

8. TodosMedicalLtd_20190328_20-F_EX-4.10_11587157_EX-4.10_Marketing Agreement_ Reseller Agreement — expected marketing vs predicted reseller (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AND RESELLER AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses primarily establish a reseller relationship, granting exclusive distribution and resale rights, detailing ordering/pricing/payment procedures, setting commercialization milestones, and defining reseller duties. While marketing support provisions are present, the substantive core governs a reseller/distribution relationship, making ‘reseller’ the precise fit.

9. PREMIERBIOMEDICALINC_05_14_2020-EX-10.2-INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AGREEMENT — expected ip vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document establishes a collaborative framework explicitly labeled as a ‘Joint Venture’ for the collective development, implementation, and commercialization of a medical treatment. Section 3 details the JV structure, including cooperative development obligations, specific funding allocations, and shared rights/royalties. While it contains substantial intellectual property licensing provisions (making license/IP the runner-up), the operative core governing the parties’ ongoing relationship, joint development efforts, and resource pooling aligns most closely with the joint_venture family.

10. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled a ‘Non-Disclosure and Non-Competition Agreement’ and contains operative clauses establishing confidentiality obligations and restrictive covenants (non-compete, non-solicit, non-diversion of customers) between a franchisee and its personnel. This directly matches the non_compete_no_solicit family.

11. DovaPharmaceuticalsInc_20181108_10-Q_EX-10.2_11414857_EX-10.2_Promotion Agreement — expected promotion vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘CO-PROMOTION AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses center on one party conducting promotional activities, sales force detailing, and marketing coordination (including a Joint Steering Committee and Marketing Sub-Committee) for a specific pharmaceutical product, along with a promotion fee structure. This aligns directly with the marketing family, which encompasses marketing and promotion services.

12. CybergyHoldingsInc_20140520_10-Q_EX-10.27_8605784_EX-10.27_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses grant the counterparty the right to advertise, market, and sell the company’s technology, while imposing obligations such as submitting annual marketing plans, meeting sales quotas, and providing promotional support. Per the marketing core guard rule, agreements whose titles name ‘Marketing’ and whose operative core centers on sales promotion and marketing services are classified as marketing, even when they include resale or distribution mechanics.

The model’s own reasoning on every failed row — the evidence it cited for the wrong family, and the failure mode that explains WHY it missed:

**1. LejuHoldingsLtd_20140121_DRS (on F-1)_EX-10.26_8473102_EX-10.26_Content License Agreement2** — expected license vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: other_fallback

The document is explicitly titled ‘Mutual Termination Agreement’ and contains standard contractual recitals and operative clauses to terminate a prior Domain Name License Agreement. It does not establish a new ongoing commercial relationship matching any of the specific contract families (e.g., license, distribution, services), making ‘other’ the correct subtype. The formal structure, mutual covenants, governing law clause, and signature blocks strongly confirm it as a binding contract.

2. ElPolloLocoHoldingsInc_20200306_10-K_EX-10.16_12041700_EX-10.16_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted franchise (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘El Pollo Loco® Franchise Development Agreement’ and contains classic franchise machinery: it grants development rights for multiple franchised restaurants within a territory, references a Franchise Disclosure Document (FDD), mandates execution of individual Franchise Agreements for each site, and outlines franchise-specific terms such as franchise fees, royalties, site approval committees, and territorial restrictions. These operative clauses and the explicit title firmly classify it under the franchise family.

3. EtonPharmaceuticalsInc_20191114_10-Q_EX-10.1_11893941_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Exclusive License and Product Development Agreement’. Its operative core centers on Section 2, which grants an exclusive right and license to products, regulatory dossiers, and background intellectual property for commercialization in a defined territory. The financial structure relies on upfront licensing fees, sales-based milestones, and running royalties, which are hallmark features of IP/license agreements. Although it contains regulatory development and manufacturing covenants, these serve as conditions and obligations ancillary to the primary grant of an exclusive license, firmly categorizing it under the license family.

4. Freecook_20180605_S-1_EX-10.3_11233807_EX-10.3_Hosting Agreement — expected hosting vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Website Design, Development and Hosting Agreement.’ The operative clauses and Exhibit A focus heavily on custom website design and development deliverables, including change orders, project timelines, rush work provisions, and a detailed multi-stage Scope of Work with specific development milestones. While Section 4 references hosting-related customer service, the substantive core and primary financial obligation center on the design and development process, making ‘development’ the most accurate subtype per the hybrid agreement weighting rules.

5. HEMISPHERX - Sales, Marketing, Distribution, and Supply Agreement — expected supply vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Sales, Marketing, Distribution, and Supply Agreement.’ Operative clauses extensively detail exclusive territorial distribution rights, purchase orders, rolling forecasts, transfer pricing, supply logistics, and quality management, which are characteristic of a distributor agreement. Exhibit 4 explicitly references the parent contract as a ‘Specialty Distributor Purchase and Service Agreement,’ confirming the substantive family.

6. Zounds Hearing, Inc. - MANUFACTURING DESIGN MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted manufacturing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MANUFACTURING, DESIGN AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses overwhelmingly govern the production, pricing, tooling, delivery, inventory, and FDA regulatory compliance of manufactured medical devices. While it references design engineering and joint marketing, these are either ancillary or expressly deferred to future separate agreements. Under the hybrid agreement rules, the operative core of manufacturing production and supply commitments dictates the ‘manufacturing’ classification.

7. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement.’ While the title references licensing and marketing, the operative clauses predominantly establish EKR as the exclusive distributor, detail sub-distributor appointments, define net sales and royalty calculations based on resale, and govern territorial sales, warehousing, and supply chain logistics. Per the hybrid agreement rules, the substantive commercial distribution and resale machinery controls the classification over the ancillary license and marketing provisions.

8. TodosMedicalLtd_20190328_20-F_EX-4.10_11587157_EX-4.10_Marketing Agreement_ Reseller Agreement — expected marketing vs predicted reseller (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘MARKETING AND RESELLER AGREEMENT’ executed between two corporate parties. The operative clauses center on granting exclusive rights to distribute and sell products, detailing purchase orders, pricing, delivery lead times, sales milestones, and quarterly reporting. While marketing activities are included, the substantive commercial machinery focuses on resale and distribution, making ‘reseller’ the best fit under the contract subtypes.

9. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled a ‘Non-Disclosure and Non-Competition Agreement’ and contains standard restrictive covenant provisions, including confidentiality obligations, covenants not to compete, non-solicitation of customers/employees, and injunctive relief clauses. This directly matches the non_compete_no_solicit family.

10. KINGPHARMACEUTICALSINC_08_09_2006-EX-10.1-PROMOTION AGREEMENT — expected promotion vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘PROMOTION AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses focus entirely on the promotion and marketing of a pharmaceutical product. Key provisions include granting co-exclusive promotion rights, establishing a Joint Commercialization Committee to direct promotional activities, detailing Launch and Annual Plans, allocating Advertising/Marketing/Educational Expenses, staffing a sales force for promotional efforts, and approving promotional materials. This aligns directly with the marketing family under the contract subtype guidelines.

11. DovaPharmaceuticalsInc_20181108_10-Q_EX-10.2_11414857_EX-10.2_Promotion Agreement — expected promotion vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘CO-PROMOTION AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses center on Valeant conducting promotional activities, deploying a dedicated sales force for detailing, managing compliance, and receiving a promotion fee based on net sales. These substantive obligations align directly with the marketing family (marketing and promotion services), which governs the agreement despite the presence of collaborative governance mechanisms like a Joint Steering Committee.

1. OLDAPIWIND-DOWNLTD_01_08_2016-EX-1.3-AGENCY AGREEMENT2 — expected agency vs predicted other (corporate_record, conf 0.85) — mode: function_over_form

The document is an ‘Agents’ Certificate’ which serves as a compliance certification and representation within the context of a securities offering (specifically referencing Regulation D and the Securities Act). While it references an underlying ‘Agency Agreement’, this specific document is a formal record/certificate executed to satisfy regulatory and contractual conditions precedent for the sale of securities. It does not contain the operative grant of agency rights itself but rather certifies compliance with laws and terms of that agreement. In legal document classification, such certificates, opinions, and compliance statements attached to or part of the closing deliverables are typically categorized as corporate records or compliance filings rather than the primary contract itself. Given the options, ‘corporate_record’ fits best as a formal record of compliance/representation in a corporate transaction, distinct from the ‘correspondence’ or the main ‘contract’. However, since it is a signed certificate defining obligations/representations, it could arguably be seen as a contract exhibit, but its primary function is evidentiary/compliance. Between ‘compliance_filing’ (usually SEC forms like 10-K) and ‘corporate_record’ (internal/closing docs), ‘corporate_record’ is the stronger fit for a closing certificate.

2. Microgenics Corporation - Collaborative Development and Commercialization Agreement — expected development vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘COLLABORATIVE DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses establish a joint research program governed by a Joint Steering Committee (JSC) and Joint Project Team (JPT), with shared responsibilities for development, regulatory filings, and commercialization. Per Rule 21, agreements with this specific title and governance structure (joint committees, joint research program) are classified as collaboration, even though they contain development machinery.

Given the construction-focused nature (‘OSP Construction’, ‘Route Feasibility’), it is a specialized service agreement. The title ‘Strategic Alliance’ is likely used for commercial framing rather than legal substance. 1. Monsanto Company - SECOND A_R EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’. Article 2 is titled ‘EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND DISTRIBUTORSHIP’ and Section 2.1 appoints Scotts as Monsanto’s ‘exclusive agent’. While the agreement contains significant marketing and distribution machinery (sales, merchandising, warehousing), the governing legal structure is that of an agency relationship where the Agent acts on behalf of the Principal (Monsanto) for specific markets. The operative clauses define the scope of this agency appointment, obligations, and commission structure. Under Rule 8, the title naming a family (‘Agency’) dictates the classification over generic commercial terms.

2. SUNTRONCORP_05_17_2006-EX-10.22-MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT — expected maintenance vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: other_fallback

The document is explicitly titled ‘MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT’ and contains operative clauses requiring the Investor to make ‘Required Capital Contributions’ (cash or subordinated loans) to maintain the Borrowers’ financial ratios for a financing agreement. While the title includes ‘Maintenance’, this refers to financial maintenance (capitalization/liquidity covenants), not software or equipment maintenance/support services. The substantive obligation is a capital contribution/guarantee arrangement to support debt financing. This does not fit any of the specific commercial contract families listed (such as license, service, supply, etc.). Therefore, per Rule 8, it is classified as ‘other’.

3. WELLSFARGOMORTGAGEBACKEDSECURITIES2006-6TRUST_05_11_2006-EX-10.3-Yield Maintenance Agreement — expected maintenance vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: other_fallback

The document is a ‘Yield Maintenance Agreement’ which serves as a Confirmation for an Interest Rate Cap Transaction between UBS AG and Wells Fargo Bank. It incorporates the ISDA Master Agreement and defines specific financial terms (fixed/floating rates, calculation amounts) for a derivative swap/cap transaction. The document is explicitly titled ‘EL POLLO LOCO® FRANCHISE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. It establishes a relationship between a Franchisor and a Developer to open multiple restaurants under the El Pollo Loco system. The operative clauses grant development rights contingent upon the execution of individual Franchise Agreements for each site, require adherence to the Franchisor’s System/Manual, and include standard franchise provisions like non-compete covenants and royalty structures (via the underlying Franchise Agreement). While it involves ‘development’ of sites, the substantive legal framework is that of a franchise agreement (specifically a multi-unit development agreement within a franchise system), not a product or software development contract. Rule 21 confirms that agreements titled as such with franchise structures are classified as franchise.

42. ArcaUsTreasuryFund_20200207_N-2_EX-99.K5_11971930_EX-99.K5_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘FORM OF BLOCKCHAIN ADMINISTRATION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ between a Fund and a Blockchain Administrator. The operative clauses (Section 1) define the Administrator’s role as an independent contractor providing ‘development and administrative services,’ including coding, smart contract maintenance, and general fund administration. While the title includes ‘Development,’ the substantive obligations are broad administrative and technical support services rather than a specific product development project with milestones or IP ownership transfer typical of a pure Development Agreement. It does not fit other specific categories like license, hosting, or outsourcing (which usually implies a broader business process shift). Therefore, it is best classified as a Service Agreement.

43. AimmuneTherapeuticsInc_20200205_8-K_EX-10.3_11967170_EX-10.3_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is explicitly titled ‘LICENSE, DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Article 2) grant an exclusive license of intellectual property rights. While the agreement contains significant development and commercialization obligations, the primary legal mechanism is the licensing of Xencor’s patents and know-how to Aimmune for those purposes. Under standard contract classification taxonomies (and CUAD conventions), such agreements are classified as License Agreements unless they are strictly joint R&D collaborations or purely development-for-hire arrangements without a core IP transfer/license grant structure.

44. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily define the Endorser’s (Arnold Schwarzenegger) obligations to lend his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm products, including specific appearances, video production, and advertising usage rights. While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, the core substantive agreement is an endorsement deal where a celebrity endorses a product line. Rule 6 identifies endorsements as a distinct family, and the title/recitals strongly support this classification over pure license or co-branding.

45. CybergyHoldingsInc_20140520_10-Q_EX-10.27_8605784_EX-10.27_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Section 2.1) grant the Marketing Affiliate the right to ‘advertise, market and sell’ the Technology. Section 3 outlines duties including marketing efforts, submitting an annual marketing plan, and adhering to brand guidelines. While it involves resale, the agreement explicitly states MA cannot remarket/redistribute for multiple users and focuses on marketing/sales activities rather than pure distribution logistics or manufacturing. Under Rule 16, a ‘Marketing Agreement’ with supply/reseller machinery stays classified as marketing because the core obligations are sales promotion and marketing services.

Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), the agreement involves purchase/resale and order terms typical of a distributor, alongside branding/promotion typical of marketing. Between distributor and marketing, the appointment as ‘exclusive distributor’ and the supply chain mechanics (purchase from PPI, sub-distributors, inventory) constitute the primary commercial relationship structure, making ‘distributor’ the best fit. 16. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

17. DYNAMEXINC_06_06_1996-EX-10.4-TRANSPORTATION SERVICES AGREEMENT — expected transportation vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AND TRANSPORTATION SERVICES AGREEMENT’. While it involves significant transportation logistics (courier services), the operative clauses emphasize joint sales and marketing efforts, co-branding under respective trade-marks, and non-solicitation of each other’s customers to protect market share. Under Rule 16 (‘MARKETING CORE GUARD’), when the title names marketing and the operative core includes sales promotion/branding/joint marketing, the agreement stays classified as marketing even with supply/logistics machinery. 8. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily focus on the Endorser (Arnold Schwarzenegger) lending his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm products (Section 2, Section 3). While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, Rule 6 specifically identifies ‘Endorsement Agreement’ as the category for celebrity/influencer deals and product endorsements. The core obligation is the endorsement of the company’s business and products.

9. HEALTHGATEDATACORP_11_24_1999-EX-10.1-HOSTING AND MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT - Escrow Agreement — expected hosting vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ESCROW AGREEMENT’ and functions as a tripartite agreement between a software Owner (Licensor), a Licensee, and an Escrow Agent (NCC). Its substantive purpose is to secure the source code of a licensed software package (‘HealthGate Electronic Journal Proprietary Software’) for release under specific conditions (e.g., bankruptcy, failure to maintain). While it involves escrow mechanics, in legal classification taxonomies (like CUAD), software escrow agreements are categorized under the ‘License’ family because they are ancillary to and define the security interests within the underlying software license relationship. It does not fit other subtypes like maintenance (which focuses on support services) or development.

10. UNITEDNATIONALBANCORP_03_03_1999-EX-99-Outsourcing Agreement with the BISYS Group, Inc. — expected outsourcing vs predicted other (correspondence, conf 0.95) — mode: function_over_form

The document is a press release announcing an agreement, not the agreement itself. It contains quotes from executives and contact information typical of corporate correspondence/PR materials. While it references an ‘Outsourcing Agreement’, the document type is clearly correspondence.

11. HEMISPHERX - Sales, Marketing, Distribution, and Supply Agreement — expected supply vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Sales, Marketing, Distribution, and Supply Agreement’. While it contains a license grant (Section II) and supply terms (Section IV), the operative core of the agreement places significant obligations on SCIEN to execute a Business Plan, manage logistics, hold inventory, provide sales forecasts, and actively promote/distribute the product in the Territory. The commercial machinery of purchase, resale, and distribution rights dominates the substantive obligations. Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when development plans are absent but commercial/resale terms are present, the distributor family is the best fit. The confidence is capped at 0.85 because the agreement is a hybrid involving both supply and licensing elements.

12. Zounds Hearing, Inc. - MANUFACTURING DESIGN MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted manufacturing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘MANUFACTURING, DESIGN AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’. While it contains marketing provisions (Section 9), the substantive operative core of the agreement revolves around the manufacturing of hearing aids by the Subcontractor for the Manufacturer. Key clauses include purchase orders for manufactured goods (Section 3), product pricing based on manufacturing costs (Section 3.3), engineering and design services related to production (Section 3.7), tooling and NRE charges (Section 3.8), delivery terms (Section 4), and regulatory compliance for medical device manufacturing (Section 14). The marketing component is secondary and described as a separate joint arrangement. Under Rule 26 (‘MARKETING TITLE WINS’), one might consider marketing, but Rule 26 explicitly carves out agreements where the title’s PRIMARY family is another specific operational service family like manufacturing. Furthermore, Rule 24 establishes that outsourcing titles win, but this is a direct manufacturing supply relationship rather than a business-process outsourcing arrangement. The dominant economic activity and legal obligations are manufacturing and supply of goods, fitting the ‘manufacturing’ subtype.

13. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is an ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement’. It contains operative clauses for licensing (Section 2.2), marketing (Section 4.6), and distribution (Section 2.1). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when the title names multiple families, we weigh the operative clauses. The agreement appoints EKR as the ‘exclusive distributor’ with rights to sell, distribute, warehouse, and appoint sub-distributors, and includes standard supply chain mechanics (purchase obligations, net sales definitions, royalties on sales). While it includes marketing and IP license elements, these are ancillary to the core commercial relationship of distributing and selling the product. Therefore, ‘distributor’ is the best fit among the specific families.

14. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. Its operative clauses (Sections 1 and 2) establish confidentiality obligations and covenants not to compete or solicit customers/employees. While it exists within a franchise context, the substantive agreement between the Franchisee and its personnel is a restrictive covenant agreement, fitting the non_compete_no_solicit subtype.

15. EhaveInc_20190515_20-F_EX-4.44_11678816_EX-4.44_License Agreement_ Reseller Agreement — expected reseller vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is titled ‘LICENSE AND RESELLER AGREEMENT’. It contains both a license grant (Section 2(b)) and an exclusive appointment for CHT to resell the solution (Section 2(a)). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when an agreement combines license and distribution/resale elements, the operative core determines the subtype. The agreement explicitly appoints CHT as a ‘reseller’ with exclusive rights to sell/sub-license in a specific field of use, includes royalty structures based on sales, audit rights for revenue verification, and marketing obligations typical of a distribution channel. While it involves software licensing, the commercial mechanism is resale/distribution. Therefore, it fits the ‘distributor’ family better than ‘license’ or ‘other’. Confidence is slightly lowered (0.85) due to the hybrid nature (License + Reseller), but the reseller machinery is dominant.

16. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses establish a joint venture structure for specific activities (AMR market development). Section 4.1 states: ‘The parties will be joint venturers only as to those activities that they jointly undertake…’. The agreement details joint ownership of IP developed during the collaboration (Section 3.1.1), shared marketing rights, and profit/loss sharing mechanisms typical of a joint venture. While the title says ‘Affiliate’, Rule 27 defines ‘affiliate’ contracts as those with referral/commission machinery (links, referral fees). This contract lacks that machinery and instead creates a formal JV entity-like relationship for product development and sales. Therefore, it falls under the ‘joint_venture’ family based on its substantive legal effect, consistent with the instruction to classify by substantive form rather than title when the title is misleading or generic.

1. Monsanto Company - SECOND A_R EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’. Article 2 is titled ‘EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND DISTRIBUTORSHIP’ and Section 2.1 appoints Scotts as Monsanto’s ‘exclusive agent’. While the agreement contains significant marketing and distribution obligations, the primary legal structure is that of an agency relationship where the Agent acts on behalf of the Principal (Monsanto) for sales and marketing services, rather than taking title to goods as a principal buyer/reseller (which would characterize a distributor or supply agreement). The operative clauses focus on the Agent’s duties to sell, promote, and manage the business for Monsanto, consistent with an Agency Agreement.

The document is explicitly titled ‘MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT’ and contains operative clauses requiring the Investor to make ‘Required Capital Contributions’ (cash or loans) to maintain the Borrowers’ financial ratios for a financing agreement. While the title includes the word ‘Maintenance’, Rule 13 specifically applies to software/tech maintenance agreements (‘Software License and Maintenance Agreement’). This document is a financial capital maintenance agreement (a form of guaranty or support agreement). It does not fit the standard definitions of license, service, or general maintenance services. It is not a joint venture, collaboration, or strategic alliance in the operational sense, but rather a specific financial obligation instrument. Therefore, it falls under ‘other’ as it fits none of the listed families (specifically excluding the tech-maintenance exception).

1. HEALTHGATEDATACORP_11_24_1999-EX-10.1-HOSTING AND MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT - Escrow Agreement — expected hosting vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ESCROW AGREEMENT’ and functions as a tripartite agreement between the software Owner, Licensee, and Escrow Agent (NCC). Its substantive purpose is to secure the source code (‘Material’) of a licensed software package for release under specific conditions (e.g., Owner bankruptcy or failure to maintain). While it involves escrow services, the core legal relationship governs the custody and conditional release of intellectual property associated with a license. It does not fit other subgroups like maintenance (which focuses on support obligations) or service (general professional services). Therefore, it is best classified as a license-related agreement.

29. ElPolloLocoHoldingsInc_20200306_10-K_EX-10.16_12041700_EX-10.16_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted franchise (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘EL POLLO LOCO® FRANCHISE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses grant the Developer rights to establish and operate franchised restaurants under the Franchisor’s system, require the execution of individual Franchise Agreements for each site, and reference the Franchise Disclosure Document. While it contains development milestones (a ‘development’ feature), Rule 21 specifically states that a ‘Franchise Development Agreement’ or similar structure where the core is granting franchise rights for developed units is classified as ‘franchise’, not ‘development’. The agreement serves as the master framework for future franchise relationships.

30. ArcaUsTreasuryFund_20200207_N-2_EX-99.K5_11971930_EX-99.K5_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘FORM OF BLOCKCHAIN ADMINISTRATION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ between a Fund and a Blockchain Administrator. The operative clauses (Section 1) define the Administrator’s role as an independent contractor providing ‘development and administrative services,’ including coding, smart contract maintenance, and general fund administration (record keeping, reporting, liaison with agents). While it contains development elements, the broader scope of administrative duties and the nature of the relationship (hiring a service provider for ongoing operational support rather than a specific R&D milestone project) aligns best with a Service Agreement. It is not a license, distribution, or joint venture. The ‘development’ aspect is part of the service delivery.

31. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily focus on the Endorser (Arnold Schwarzenegger) lending his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm’s products (Section 2, Section 3). It includes standard endorsement machinery such as personal appearances, approval of advertising materials, FTC compliance affidavits, exclusivity/non-competition regarding competing dietary supplements, and compensation via royalties and stock for these endorsement services. While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, the core substantive obligation is the celebrity endorsement.

32. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses define a joint development and commercialization relationship for AMR products. Section 3 details joint development efforts, joint ownership of IP, coordinated marketing/sales roles, and profit-sharing mechanisms. Section 4.1 explicitly states the parties are ‘joint venturers’ only for these specific activities. Under Rule 21 (‘Development Versus Collaboration…’), a collaborative agreement with joint R&D/development machinery (joint steering, shared IP, joint product development) is classified as collaboration. The ‘affiliate’ title refers to the business relationship structure rather than an affiliate/referral program (Rule 27), and the core obligations are collaborative development and commercialization.

1. Monsanto Company - SECOND A_R EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.86) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’ and contains an ‘EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND DISTRIBUTORSHIP’ section with explicit appointment of an exclusive agent (Section 2.1). While it includes marketing provisions, the operative core centers on agency/appointment and distribution, indicating the primary contract family is agency (not marketing).

2. MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement — expected marketing vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.63) — mode: other_fallback

Document is a binding contract titled ‘Remarketing Agreement’ governing remarketing of MetLife securities and appointment of remarketing agents, with sections on obligations, pricing, indemnification, and termination. It does not fit any of the specified contract subtypes (affiliate, agency, collaboration, development, distributor, license, marketing, sponsorship, etc.), so it is best classified as ‘other’ within contract.

3. LECLANCHÉ S.A. - JOINT DEVELOPMENT AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.72) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled “Joint Development and Marketing Agreement” and contains development-focused provisions (Phase 1 market evaluation, design and development of products, a royalty-free license for design/development, joint responsibilities for development and marketing, and IP handling). While marketing components are present (Oak Ridge responsibilities for sales/marketing), the operative core centers on collaborative development and joint R&D efforts, which aligns with the Development contract family. No explicit joint venture, license-only, or solely marketing framework overrides this, so development is the best fit with moderate confidence given the hybrid nature.

4. Magenta Therapeutics, Inc. - Master Development and Manufacturing Agreement — expected manufacturing vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.92) — mode: family_confusion

Document is a Master Development and Manufacturing Agreement with explicit Development Work, Development Specifications, and Project Plans governing development services and product manufacturing. The operative clauses center on development activities (and associated regulatory/compliance work) alongside manufacturing, which, per the guidelines, yields a Development contract rather than a pure manufacturing or license contract.

5. VERTEXENERGYINC_08_14_2014-EX-10.24-OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT — expected maintenance vs predicted outsourcing (contract, conf 0.82) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT’ and between Owner and Operator, appointing the Operator to manage, operate, and maintain the Rail Facility (section 2.1 ‘Engagement’). This structure is characteristic of an outsourcing arrangement where an external party performs operational/maintenance functions for the Owner, rather than a pure maintenance, license, or marketing agreement. The core provisions govern service delivery, costs, and liability related to operation of the facility, supporting the outsourcing classification.

6. TELEGLOBEINTERNATIONALHOLDINGSLTD_03_29_2004-EX-10.10-CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT — expected maintenance vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.72) — mode: family_confusion

1. Monsanto Company - SECOND A_R EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Second Amended and Restated Exclusive Agency and Marketing Agreement’ and details the appointment of the Agent as Monsanto’s exclusive agent for marketing and distribution of Roundup Products in the Lawn and Garden Market. The content includes specific agency duties, obligations, and terms, clearly indicating it is an agency agreement. The high confidence is supported by the explicit references to agency roles, obligations, and the contractual language consistent with agency agreements.

3. LECLANCHÉ S.A. - JOINT DEVELOPMENT AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Joint Development and Marketing Agreement’ and describes a collaboration between Leclanché and Oak Ridge involving joint market evaluation, development, and marketing efforts. The operative clauses focus on joint activities, market evaluation, and shared responsibilities, indicating a collaboration or cooperation agreement. The presence of joint development and marketing activities aligns with the ‘collaboration’ subtype. The confidence is high due to the explicit collaboration language and the focus on joint efforts, but not 0.90+ because the title also emphasizes development and marketing, which could suggest other subtypes, though the operative clauses strongly support ‘collaboration’.

1. HEALTHGATEDATACORP_11_24_1999-EX-10.1-HOSTING AND MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT - Escrow Agreement — expected hosting vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a standard form escrow agreement (NCC Escrow International) for software source code, which is a formal contract between three parties (Owner, Licensee, and NCC). The operative clauses cover deposit, release events, confidentiality, verification, and fees — all characteristic of a service agreement for escrow support. The document is clearly a contract, and the subtype ‘service’ best fits this escrow arrangement, as it is a general professional/support service. No competing signals are present, so confidence is high.

2. TUNIUCORP_03_06_2014-EX-10-COOPERATION AGREEMENT — expected collaboration vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal cooperation agreement (2014 amendment) between two Chinese companies, titled ‘Cooperation Agreement’. The operative clauses describe Party B providing technical services and business consultancy to Party A, including development, operation, and maintenance of an internet platform, with exclusive cooperation and service fees based on profits. There is no development plan or milestones, and the core is ongoing service provision rather than a standalone development project. The IP ownership clause (12.3) is typical for service agreements where the service provider owns developed IP. The document matches the ‘service’ subtype (general professional/support services) more closely than ‘development’ or ‘consulting’, as the services are broad and ongoing. Confidence is 0.85 due to some ambiguity with development elements, but the overall structure and lack of development-specific machinery support ‘service’.

1. HEALTHGATEDATACORP_11_24_1999-EX-10.1-HOSTING AND MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT - Escrow Agreement — expected hosting vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal ‘ESCROW AGREEMENT’ (specifically STD001Y2K.UK) between an Owner, a Licensee, and an escrow agent (NCC). Its substantive purpose is to secure the source code of a licensed software package (‘HealthGate Electronic Journal Proprietary Software’) for the benefit of the licensee in case of default or bankruptcy by the owner. The operative clauses define duties related to the deposit, verification, and release of this intellectual property/materials. While it involves third-party custodianship, the core legal relationship and subject matter revolve around the licensing of the underlying software and the protection of that license’s value through IP escrow. It does not fit other specific contract families like maintenance (which focuses on support services), development (creating new IP), or general service agreements. Therefore, it falls under the license family as it governs the security and continuity of a software license.

2. NATIONALPROCESSINGINC_07_18_1996-EX-10.4-SPONSORSHIP AGREEMENT — expected sponsorship vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Sponsorship Agreement’, but the substantive operative clauses explicitly establish an agency relationship. Section 1.1 states ‘NCB appoints NPC… as NCB’s sole agent’ to provide processing services and enter into contracts on NCB’s behalf. The recitals confirm NPC will ‘act as an agent of NCB’. Under Rule 26, a marketing-named title whose core is not pure promotion (here, it is service provision via agency) does not override the substantive machinery; however, this is not a marketing agreement at all, it is a service/agency agreement mislabeled in the title. The governing legal structure is Agency.

3. LOOKSMARTLTD_07_20_2012-EX-99.(D)(I)-SPONSORSHIP AGREEMENT — expected sponsorship vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Sponsorship Agreement’ but its substantive content governs a consortium of investors (‘Sponsors’) pooling capital through a special purpose vehicle (‘Purchaser’) to execute a tender offer. The operative clauses establish joint governance (unanimous consent requirements), shared equity commitments, pro-rata distribution of assets and termination fees, and specific performance remedies for defaulting co-investors. This structure constitutes a joint venture or project collaboration among the sponsors. Per Rule 12, while that rule specifically addresses SEC Joint Filing Agreements, the broader classification logic for agreements establishing a joint enterprise with shared risk/reward and governance points to ‘joint_venture’. The term ‘Sponsorship’ here refers to financial sponsorship/backing of the bid, not event sponsorship. It fits the ‘joint_venture’ family better than ‘sponsorship’ (which implies branding/event support) or ‘collaboration’ (which is often looser R&D/cooperation). The CUAD corpus convention files these types of tender offer sponsor agreements under Joint Venture.

4. CHINARECYCLINGENERGYCORP_11_14_2013-EX-10.6-Cooperation Agreement — expected collaboration vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a ‘Project Cooperation Agreement’ where two parties (Party A and Party B) jointly invest in and operate a specific industrial project (CDQ and waste heat power generation). The agreement outlines shared responsibilities for investment, construction, operation, and profit/loss sharing (e.g., sharing policy rebates 50/50, defined service fees based on output). This structure of pooling resources to undertake a specific business undertaking with shared governance and economic benefits fits the definition of a Joint Venture. While it involves elements of development and maintenance, the core legal relationship is the joint venture entity/project structure itself. Confidence is slightly lowered from 0.90+ because it is a single-project JV rather than a permanent corporate JV, but it clearly falls under the joint_venture family per corpus conventions for such cooperation agreements.

5. OLDAPIWIND-DOWNLTD_01_08_2016-EX-1.3-AGENCY AGREEMENT2 — expected agency vs predicted other (correspondence, conf 0.85) — mode: function_over_form

The document is an ‘Agents’ Certificate’, which serves as a certification or representation letter regarding compliance with securities laws in connection with an underlying Agency Agreement. While it references and relies on the terms of an ‘Agency Agreement’ (making ‘agency’ the relevant contract family/subtype for context), the document itself is a certificate/letter of representation rather than the operative agreement establishing the agency relationship. It functions as correspondence/notices between parties to confirm status. The subtype ‘agency’ is assigned because the substantive legal framework being certified is the agency arrangement.

6. AgapeAtpCorp_20191202_10-KA_EX-10.1_11911128_EX-10.1_Supply Agreement — expected supply vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ODM - SUPPLY AGREEMENT’ and functions as a supply agreement where the Manufacturer supplies products to the Customer. The operative clauses (Section 13) appoint the Customer as the ‘sole and exclusive agent for the promotion, sales, marketing, distribution and administration’ of the products. Crucially, Schedule B establishes ‘Minimum Annual Product Performance Requirements’ defined as ‘Agreed Quantity of Units to be purchased per Annum’, which creates a binding purchase obligation characteristic of a distributor relationship rather than a pure agency or service arrangement. While it contains marketing language, the core commercial mechanism is the supply and resale/purchase of goods.

7. HEMISPHERX - Sales, Marketing, Distribution, and Supply Agreement — expected supply vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Sales, Marketing, Distribution, and Supply Agreement’. The operative clauses establish a commercial relationship where HEMISPHERX supplies the product to SCIEN, and SCIEN is granted an exclusive license to sell, market, and distribute the product in a specific territory (GCC states). The document is a press release announcing an agreement, which falls under the ‘correspondence’ class (letters, notices, announcements). But wait, often in these datasets, if the text contains the operative clauses or is clearly the agreement, it’s a contract. Here, it is clearly a press release. ‘United National Bancorp Enters Into…’. It quotes the CEO. It has contact info. This is correspondence.

Rule 26 states that when a title names marketing alongside other families, if the core is promotion/placement it stays marketing; however, here the core is clearly production/manufacturing. 1. HEALTHGATEDATACORP_11_24_1999-EX-10.1-HOSTING AND MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT - Escrow Agreement — expected hosting vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘ESCROW AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses establish a tripartite arrangement where NCC Escrow International provides escrow services (holding source code, verification, release upon events) for an Owner and Licensee. This is a contract for services, fitting the ‘service’ subtype. No other subtype (e.g., license, development) is indicated by the content.

2. INNOVIVA,INC_08_07_2014-EX-10.1-COLLABORATION AGREEMENT — expected collaboration vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘COLLABORATION AGREEMENT’ and its operative core involves a joint drug development program, including a Development Plan, Joint Steering Committee, Joint Project Committee, development milestones, and funding for development activities. Per Rule 21, a collaborative development and commercialization agreement with development machinery (such as development plans and joint steering committees) is classified as development, not collaboration. The document is titled ‘JOINT DEVELOPMENT AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’, which suggests a collaboration between the parties for development and marketing purposes. The agreement outlines the parties’ responsibilities, including joint development of products and marketing efforts. While the agreement also mentions marketing, the primary focus appears to be on joint development, with provisions for market evaluation, product development, and intellectual property protection. According to rule 10, when one of the named families is development and the operative clauses contain development machinery, development is preferred over the commercial family. In this case, the agreement’s operative clauses contain development plans, milestones, and joint research programs, which supports the classification as a development agreement. However, the presence of marketing provisions and the title’s mention of marketing reduce the confidence level to 0.85, as the agreement could also be argued to be a marketing agreement.

The document is titled ‘NETWORK AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’ and outlines the terms of an agreement between National CineMedia, LLC and Digital Cinema Destinations Corp. regarding the provision of advertising services, including digital content and lobby promotions, to be displayed in movie theaters. The agreement includes provisions for the delivery of advertising content, equipment installation and maintenance, and revenue sharing. The contract_subtype is classified as ‘marketing’ because the primary purpose of the agreement is to facilitate the display of advertisements in movie theaters, which is a key aspect of marketing.
